lines: My schedule is very <wavy>flexible</wavy>. Mostly because nobody put anything on it.
I asked the job board for a sign. It pointed at the broom.
Apparently looking busy is not a trade. I checked twice.
I offered to supervise the chickens. They already had management.
The farmer said I needed experience, so I watched him work all afternoon.
I finally found steady work. The chair had one short leg.
Someone told me to follow my calling. It must have taken the other road.
I tried to take a day off, but nobody noticed the difference.
The barrel hired me for storage. The pay was inside the barrel.
I asked whether sweeping leads anywhere. The broom said across the room.
My career plan is simple. First, find a career plan.
The village has plenty of openings. Most of them are holes in the fence.
I told everyone I was between jobs. They asked which two.
A trader called me available. I called him observant.
I volunteered to ring the bell. They said emergencies only, so I waited for lunch.
I tried farming once. The crops preferred someone with a schedule.
The smith offered me an apprenticeship. Then he saw me hold the hot end.
I can do any job badly enough to appreciate the expert.
My workstation is wherever I set down the bucket.
I asked for honest work. Someone handed me a full compost bin.
I nearly found my calling yesterday, but it was meant for someone else.
The good thing about odd jobs is that nobody expects even hours.
I told the broom I wanted a promotion. It put me in charge of the dustpan.
I am not unemployed. I am waiting for the village to invent my position.
My greatest skill is looking occupied when someone carries a shovel.
